summary: Current orchestration frameworks can encode roles, graph transitions, persistence, triggers, and checks as versioned code. The implementation feature to look for is an inspectable state machine, not merely a list of agent personas.

items.text: LangGraph's Graph API defines nodes, normal and conditional edges, entry points, and loops in code; compiled graphs expose an explicit execution topology that can be versioned and tested.
CrewAI Flows provide event-driven start and listener methods, structured state, routing, and persistence, allowing a repository to encode which role runs after which verified event.
Microsoft AutoGen GraphFlow represents sequential, parallel, conditional, and looping agent execution as a directed graph; its graph structure makes handoffs and termination paths explicit.
Temporal Workflows persist event history and support retries, timers, signals, and deterministic replay, supplying durable control flow when an agent pipeline spans failures or long waits.
GitHub Actions binds repository workflows to pull-request, push, schedule, manual, and external events, so an agent pipeline and its triggering conditions can be reviewed beside the code it changes.
